titre: How Many Continents Are There? It Depends on the Country You Ask In
accroche: A French student learns six continents in school, an American seven, and the Olympic rings count only five.
contenu_vulgarise:
Ask a French student and an American student how many continents Earth has: the first will probably answer six, the second seven. Neither learned their geography badly. Both answers are taught as self-evident in their own country, and the division of the globe into continents is a convention rather than a fact settled once and for all.

## The Mechanism

The seven-continent model (Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, Oceania) is taught in most English-speaking countries, as well as in China, India, and other Asian countries. It counts Europe and Asia as two separate continents, even though they form a single continuous landmass, and it separates the two Americas, though they are joined by the Isthmus of Panama. In Russia and in much of Eastern Europe, six continents are used by merging Europe and Asia into a single Eurasia, but keeping the two Americas distinct. In France and most of the French-speaking world, as well as in Greece and in Romance-speaking countries, it is the reverse: also six continents, but obtained by unifying the two Americas and separating Europe and Asia. A five-continent variant, reflected in the 1913 Olympic flag with its five rings, starts from this last model and removes Antarctica, which is mostly uninhabited.

None of these divisions rests on a single criterion. The boundary between Europe and Asia is a historical and cultural construct: in 1725, Philip Johan von Strahlenberg was the first to depart from the classical Don boundary, drawing the line along the Volga, then the Obshchy Syrt and the Ural Mountains. The Caucasus is placed in Europe or Asia for political, economic, and historical-cultural reasons. The word itself is translated from the Latin *terra continens*, “dry land”: a stretch of land uninterrupted by the sea, a definition that the separation of Europe and Asia, a single continuous landmass, already fails to respect.

## The Shift

The received idea would have it that somewhere there exists a correct number of continents, which schools convey more or less faithfully depending on the country. That number does not exist. The division of the globe into continents is not a geographic fact to be discovered, it is a cultural convention to be chosen, and French-speaking, English-speaking, and Slavic countries have not made the same choice.

The United Nations itself stays cautious: its official statistical classification of countries and territories (M49) speaks of “geographic regions” based on “continental regions.” A note on the page specifies that the scheme rests on six continental regions, subdivided into 22 sub-regions. The detailed list places countries under Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania, with the Americas counted as a single block, and Antarctica appears there as a separate entry, with no parent region. An organization whose mission is precisely to compare the countries of the entire world has thus preferred a practical statistical division to a firm answer on a question that schools nevertheless present as self-evident.

repere.texte: The regional scheme of the UN's official statistical classification (M49) rests, according to a note on the page, on six continental regions; the detailed list places countries under Africa, the Americas (a single block), Asia, Europe, and Oceania, and lists Antarctica separately, with no parent region.
repere.source: United Nations, Statistics Division, Standard Country or Area Codes for Statistical Use (M49)

carte.punch: A French person and an American did not learn the same number of continents: both are right.
carte.idee: Seven continents in most English-speaking countries, six by merging Europe and Asia (Russia) or the two Americas (France), five by excluding Antarctica (Olympic rings). The Europe-Asia boundary is a historical and cultural construct.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: Details the seven-continent model of English-speaking countries and the six-continent model with a unified Eurasia, used mostly in Russia and parts of Eastern Europe.

quiz.question: Why is there no single, universally accepted number of continents?
choix: Because plate tectonics regularly changes the number of distinct landmasses
Because the division into continents is a cultural convention, with no geological criterion that imposes itself
Because modern satellites have revealed new landmasses that old maps ignored
Because each country is free to claim a territory as a separate continent for political purposes
quiz.explication: No geological rule distinguishes Europe from Asia, a single continuous landmass, any more clearly than North America from South America, joined by the Isthmus of Panama: the division adopted depends on historical conventions specific to each school tradition, not on tectonics or satellite imagery.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the current line of the boundary between Europe and Asia, along the Urals and the Caucasus, rest on?
choix: On a 19th-century geological survey establishing a clear tectonic discontinuity between the two continental masses
On an agreement between Russia and the Western European powers signed at the Congress of Vienna in 1815
On a proposal by the Swedish officer Philip Johan von Strahlenberg, in 1725, which departs from the classical Don boundary
On the boundary of the Volga drainage basin, the only natural criterion recognized by the geographers of the time
quiz_supplementaire.explication: In 1725 Strahlenberg is the first to depart from the classical Don boundary, drawing the line along the Volga and then the Ural Mountains. The current boundary is a historical and cultural construct, not a feature of the terrain.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In Russia and in much of Eastern Europe, how is a six-continent model obtained?
choix: By removing Antarctica from the count, for lack of a permanent population
By merging Africa and Asia along the Isthmus of Suez
By unifying the two Americas into a single continent, while keeping Europe and Asia distinct
By unifying Europe and Asia into a single Eurasia, while keeping the two Americas distinct
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Russian model merges Europe and Asia into a single Eurasia but keeps the two Americas separate, the reverse of the French-speaking model, which unifies the Americas while separating Europe and Asia.
